accepted_edits.reason: the edits are the answers recorded against the content and design findings of 22 November

findings.reason: a node dispatched to §37 runs its own gate green with no code change, so the section's 1.5 hours buy nothing and its negative control is the only case that can fail.
findings.text: §37's three cases (two resolutions list the plans directory once, adding a file adds exactly one listing, a duplicate canonical identity is refused) all already hold at the base revision, because `resources._ENTRY_NAMES` holds each directory's entry names keyed on `metadata_index._dir_identity` and was landed in `7e13a8f0a5`, an ancestor of the cited `319b74cb95`

findings.reason: the section aims at a cost that is already gone and misses the measured one, so its repair cannot move the figure it cites and the author must retarget the per-entry stamping or descope the section.
findings.text: §37's Why reads the cited 5,297 stat calls as the plans directory "re-list[ed] ... on every resource resolution", but at revision `319b74cb95` the glob is already cached in `_ENTRY_NAMES` and the 5,297 calls are `file_memo.file_signature` re-stamps of every sibling entry, which the section's "list the directory once" endpoint leaves untouched

findings.reason: a node literal to the sentence must either move the version check after the write, losing the conflict guard that refuses a stale write, or report the endpoint unachievable; the endpoint should state one parse of the written document plus the pre-write read the version check requires.
findings.text: §38's Deliverable requires "the version check, the heading guard and the section-coverage check all read that one parse" of the document the write produced, but the expected-version check gates the write and must read the document as it stood (`_write_state_locked` parses the pre-write text before any mutation), so the version check cannot read a parse of the written document

response_events.note: section 37 is restated as a bound on a warm read's stat calls that holds as the directory grows, measured at the base first, so a node cannot pass with no change
section 37 no longer targets the directory listing, which is already reused; it bounds the per-entry stats the warm profile counted
section 38 now states one read of the stored document for the version check and one parse of the document written, and requires the stale-write refusal unchanged

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited fragment `docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-costs-what-changed/arcwc-find-where-a-plan-read-spends-ten-times-its-parse.html` resolves, `docs/plans/the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches.html` resolves at 904,485 bytes, revision `319b74cb95` resolves and is an ancestor of HEAD, and every declared write-path module exists.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §37's three cases all hold on the base revision, so the section's gate cannot fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each arm's log is placed under the run directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`), which is durable and re-openable, and the timed arms run on all_debug.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames and the section prose carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — §37's stated root cause is contradicted by the code at the cited revision, and §38's deliverable requires the version check to read a parse of the document the write produced.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of s35–s38 states one deliverable, and §38's "every refusal is still raised with the same text" is a preservation constraint on that deliverable, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s35–s38 add no depends-on entry and none is operationally missing: every premise they cite (§10's profile, §22's index-backed ref read) has landed, so no unlanded upstream holds them.
